cohort: The study included 1371 singleton pregnant women with a-thalassemia and 680 non-thalassemia singleton pregnant women as a control group during the same period.
finding: Pregnant women with a-thalassemia experienced more pregnancy and delivery complications, lower hemoglobin levels, and lower neonatal delivery weight and hemoglobin compared to those without a-thalassemia.
mod_finding: The incidence of caesarean section was higher in pregnant women with a-thalassemia compared to the control group.
birth_weight: Delivery weight was measured, with lower weights observed in the a-thalassemia group.
